pillars.subtitle: Unforgettable evenings
pillars.text: We believe a bar is only as good as how it makes you feel. Your name gets remembered, your usual gets noticed, and nobody who walks in alone stays that way for long.

pillars.subtitle: A place that holds you
pillars.text: Dark wood, warm lamps and a record that was chosen on purpose. The room is built to slow you down, so one drink quietly becomes the best part of your week.

title: Serious drinks.

partners.subtitle: Together with growers, makers and musicians who share our obsession, we build evenings that delight.
list: A small-batch rye made to our spec, aged in barrels we picked ourselves and poured nowhere else in town.
Coastal herbs and citrus from one family farm, in season and delivered the same morning they are picked.
Our resident selectors, who fill the listening corner with rare vinyl every Thursday and Sunday night.
The single-origin beans behind The Night Shift, roasted a few streets away and ground to order.

title: Meet the
crew
crewPage.subtitle: The people turning long shifts into unforgettable nights.
crewPage.text: From ice carvers to record diggers, our crew is as lively as the room itself. This is the team that obsesses over every pour and every moment, making sure each guest is looked after properly.

signatures.text: My go-to drink whenever I visit this place. Not just for the bitterness, the spice or the strength, but for the story you shared with me. I started to fall in love with it, and that's why I keep coming back: to feel the care you put into every drink, to listen to your voice, and most of all, to see you.

Your newest experiment. It opens with a strong orange flavor and finishes bitter, which makes me wonder about your life story. It isn't spicy anymore, and there's some sweetness in it now, but it still feels sad.
A layered shooter from our classic list, lit at the bar and gone in one go.

the-ice-program.title: Inside Our Obsessive New Ice Program
body: Clear ice is a slow business. Our new freezer works from the bottom up, pushing air and impurities away for three days before we cut a single block by hand.
The result melts more slowly, looks better in the glass and lets a stirred drink stay itself for longer. It is also, we admit, a little ridiculous. We are keeping it.

last-ember-joins-the-list.title: “Last Ember” Joins the House List
body: After eleven versions and one small incident with the smoke gun, Last Ember has earned its place at the top of the list.
It is built on our private rye barrel, finished with burnt orange and stirred until the room goes quiet. Come and tell us if we got it right.

six-years-of-red-hour.title: Six Years of Red Hour
body: It started as a way to fill the quiet hour before eight. Six years later, Red Hour is the reason people leave work on time.
This autumn the aperitivo blend shifts to blood orange. The price, the playlist and the regulars stay exactly the same.

city-guide-names-scafe.title: City Guide Names Scafe a Bar to Watch
body: We try not to read our own reviews, but this one was pinned to the staff room wall before the ink had dried.
Thanks to everyone who has ever waited patiently for a stirred drink. The compliment belongs to the room as much as the crew.

meet-the-barrel.title: Meet Our First Private Barrel
body: We drove out to Ember & Oak with six samples, two opinions and no intention of agreeing. Five hours later we had picked one barrel.
It makes up the backbone of the rye drinks this year. When it is gone, it is gone.

a-room-with-low-light.title: A Room With Low Light
body: Nobody ever fell for a bar under fluorescent tubes. A short note on the lamps, the wood and the two years we spent getting the room to feel like nine o'clock.
